scope: Corollary 3.4 (Large generating footprints) of the manuscript “Logarithmic Relative Fluctuations in the Weakly Disordered Planar Ising Model” (preprints/Logarithmic-Relative-Fluctuations-in-the-Weakly-Disordered-Planar-Ising-Model-October-5-2026/critical-relative-second-moment-weak-random-bond-ising.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ec0e1bb240b41be6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Retain the animal footprint of a connected coefficient before projecting onto constants. For background coefficients from the small-entry expansion whose footprint has physical diameter at least D, the total absolute sum at a fixed output anchor is at most CLδe−cD/R . The same gain can be retained together with any fixed number of specified input norm factors, including marked factors. On a torus of side N, writing m = N/R, the total absolute sum of small-expansion scalar terms whose footprints wrap or fail to fit in a chart of fixed relative size is at most CLδm2e−cm. Here m is sufficiently large relative to the fixed halos. Pure bad scalar terms have chart footprints and do not contribute to this last sum.
